headline: Full-time work reaches 84.2 %, well above regional and overall levels.
how_to_read: Flows run from all respondents (left) to employed or not employed (middle) and then to detailed situation (right); width is the share of respondents. Both branch totals are hidden, so branches show as lower bounds (≥) and a hatched "Hidden" flow leaves "Respondents" directly.
key_findings: Full-time work accounts for 84.2 % of respondents.
Other employment, not seeking work, students, retirees and other situations are all absent; part-time, self-employed and seeking work are hidden.
benchmark: Full-time work is 9.6 pp above Asia (74.6 %) and 9.3 pp above all schools (74.9 %). Total employment cannot be compared, as it is hidden for this school.
caveats: With n = 19, each person moves the percentages by several points, and both totals are hidden (fewer than 3 people).
